title: Cohort onboarding and escalation flowbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working flowbook for onboarding small cohorts, scheduling progressive exposure, and handling first-line escalations during canaries and A/B experiments for LLM-serving features. It is intentionally prescriptive at the ops level (who does what, in what order) and lightweight on gating math — those live in the telemetry playbook.

Scope and intent:
- For cross-functional features (product + infra + SRE + ML) where model/serving changes are part of a user-visible experience.
- Intended for low-to-medium risk canaries (1%–10% exposure) and early A/B cohorts. High-risk or legal/regulatory changes should go through the formal signoff path (legal/security).
- Focus on minimizing blast radius while collecting signal for quality and cost.

Quick summary (one-line run):
1) Register experiment in shared tracker and assign a traffic steward.
2) Run internal smoke + guard probes at 0% -> 0.1% (synthetic) -> 1% -> target exposure.
3) Observe telemetry windows at each step; use conservative circuit breakers.
4) If guard fails, run rollback, postmortem, and patch. If unstable but non-fatal, quarantine cohort and open mitigation.

Roles and responsibilities (practical):
- Traffic steward (usually product engineer): owns cohort allocation, communication, and running the exposure checklist.
- Model steward (ML): responsible for model variant health (per-token quality metrics, hallucination rates, latency distributions).
- Infra/SRE: enforces latency/circuit-breaker limits, capacity scaling, and can perform immediate traffic cut.
- Observability owner: monitors experiment telemetry and runs the analysis template during the observation windows.
- Customer success/oncall escalation: customer-facing comms if visible impact is detected.

Key concepts and novel primitives (team jargon to adopt):
- Guardian probe: a short, deterministic synthetic workload that hits critical code paths (e.g., long context attention + embedding endpoint) to detect regression modes not visible in user traffic. Run at each exposure step.
- Drift sentinel: a lightweight continuous metric track (e.g., change in top-5 token distribution for a set of anchor prompts) to detect semantic drift early.
- Quarantine slice: a targeted isolate (by region or user tier) to which we immediately route problematic traffic for deeper inspection without full rollback.

Pre-roll checklist (must be green before 0.1%):
- Experiment registered with hypothesis, primary metrics, and owner in tracker.
- Canary variant pinned and artifactized (model version, container digest).
- Feature flagging path validated and tested in staging.
- Guardian probes written and reviewed (3 synthetic cases at minimum).
- Smoke test runbook updated with expected outputs and tolerances.
- SLO/circuit-breaker thresholds pre-declared and uploaded to the canary config.
- Pager routing verified (who gets auto-notified at 0.1%, 1%, etc.).

Exposure schedule (template):
- Step 0: Phantom/synthetic validation (internal only) — run guardian probe. Wait 30m.
- Step 1: 0.1% synthetic (non-customer traffic) — run probes + latency checks. Wait 1h.
- Step 2: 1% real traffic (or 1000 sessions) — monitor in 15m windows (3 windows).
- Step 3: 5% exposure (90m observation).
- Step 4: Target exposure (ramp to desired cohort).
Notes: do not skip synthetic steps for model changes that touch tokenizer/kv cache/attention ops.

Telemetry and primary signals (what to watch):
- Safety/quality: hallucination rate on anchor prompts, answer validity score, user cancellation rate.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 token-stream latencies and tail event counts.
- Cost: tokens per session and inferred per-request GPU utilization.
- Error budget: 5xx counts, timeouts, OOMs normalized per 1000 requests.
- Business metrics: click-through, conversion, retention as appropriate (lagging, used post-stable).

Circuit-breaker thresholds (recommended starting points):
- Immediate abort (hard cut): p95 latency > 2x baseline OR 5xx rate increases > 3x in 5m window OR critical safety regression on anchor prompts.
- Pause/quarantine: p95 > 1.5x baseline OR small but persistent safety drift OR cost > 1.3x expected.
- Soft alert: p95 > 1.2x baseline OR elevated error jitter.
These are suggestions — each experiment must include final thresholds in the registration step.

Escalation matrix (practical):
- Tier 0 (auto): infra circuit triggers (hard cut). Infra + steward + oncall paged.
- Tier 1 (within 15m): steward triages, runs guard probes, looks at logs, may quarantine slice.
- Tier 2 (within 30–60m): model and SRE deep dive — decide rollback vs mitigation.
- Tier 3 (within 2h): leadership and CS involvement if customers impacted; customer comms drafted.

Sample decision flows (short scenarios):
1) Scenario: p95 latency spikes by 2.2x after ramp to 1%
   Action: infra auto-cut -> steward notified -> steward re-runs smaller guardian probe -> if spike reproduces in probe, keep cut and open rollback PR; if not, resume at 0.1% with extended window.

2) Scenario: hallucination rate increases on anchor prompts but latency normal
   Action: model steward runs quick A/B on synthetic slices; if regression consistent, quarantine region and rollback model variant in that region; open immediate evaluation ticket and notify product for comms planning.

Guard rails for A/B comparisons (do not conflate noise):
- Always keep a control stream sampled at the same time and region as treatment.
- Use pre-declared primary metric and a second safety metric (both locked during the run).
- Avoid mixing rollout exposure with feature toggles that change prompt templates or post-processing simultaneously.

Communication template (steward uses this for Slack + email):
- Subject: [Canary] <experiment id> — running -> 1% -> observing (owner: X)
- Snapshot: what changed (model/container), exposure %, key metrics (p95, 5xx, primary metric), next step planned, who is oncall.
- If rollback: short explanation, what was cut, ETA for investigation, customer impact (if any).

Postmortem and measurement cadence:
- If gated rollback or >1h downtime: run a short incident review within 2 days and a full writeup in Confluence within 7 days.
- If experiment completes normally: owner publishes a 1–2 page result doc (hypothesis, numbers, decision) and tags product and ML.

Templates and artifacts to attach when registering an experiment:
- Experiment brief (1 paragraph hypothesis).
- Short list of anchor prompts (for drift sentinel and guardian probes).
- Telemetry dashboard link and alert links.
- Expected exposure plan (times and percentages).
- Rollback playbook link (exact steps to cut traffic).

Open questions and known TODOs (work to do in next 6 weeks):
- Define automated quarantine routing (current flow is manual; we should add a one-click UI in Console).
- Add standard guardian probe library (templates for classification, long-context, reranker).
- Storage of anchor prompt reference outputs for drift comparisons — where to persist canonical baseline?
- Flesh out cost-aware gating (dynamic thresholds if cost spikes but quality unchanged).

Short checklist for the steward when the alarm rings:
- Verify whether infra auto-cut occurred.
- Re-run guardian probe(s) and capture results.
- Check logs for region-specific anomalies and user-tier patterns.
- If unsure, quarantine slice and escalate to Tier 2.

Notes to self (rough, keep in doc):
- Avoid overloading product owners with low-signal alerts — make alerting tiered and include clear examples of "actionable changes" in the template.
- This doc should live next to the telemetry playbook and the rollout runbook index.
- Next workshop: run tabletop with SRE + ML + product on 2026-03-05 to exercise an artificial hallucination regression.

Appendix: quick links (examples)
- Canary registration template: https://confluence.redwood/example/canary-register
- Automated cut runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/211

End of file.
